grading: Manual semantic review against contract-traced checks after first generation; per-cell grading.json contains concrete evidence.
comparison: Current method-based-report and shared foundations versus no installed skill, using Claude CLI default configuration. This is not a Codex-versus-Claude or previous-version-versus-new-version benchmark.

isolation.generation_workspaces: Temporary directories outside git; moved here after generation

metric_definitions.mean_pass_rate: Mean of per-case retained discriminating checks, one per case; all were selected after reviewing outputs. Not an overall quality score or an out-of-sample estimate.
metric_definitions.mean_total_tokens: CLI input_tokens + output_tokens, excluding cache creation/read tokens; not full context consumption

observed_benefits: Both action-oriented with-skill outputs name proposed accountable roles for individual decisions; neither baseline output does so consistently.
The comparison-only with-skill output leaves internal credential applicability unknown; baseline asserts it applies internally.
shared_passes_not_scored: Mechanism explanation, dependency sequencing, comparison-only scope and several uncertainty checks passed in both arms; retained as diagnostics rather than inflating the discriminating score.
shared_gaps_not_scored: Both programme-friction outputs overstate readiness from credential/training evidence.
The commercial test remains incomplete: with-skill invents contracting/invoicing arrangements; baseline omits relevant costs and responsibilities.
Both comparison outputs make unsupported assumptions about internal application-support ownership or organisation. These are reachable criteria and real gaps, not invalid assertions.
limitations: One run per case; three synthetic short reports; no variability estimate or causal proof of a general improvement.
Checks were authored and selected after outputs, as required by project workflow; confirm on new cases before treating the rates as predictive.
Whole skill/foundation context differs between arms; the experiment does not isolate the new diagnosis-to-action paragraph.
The existing harness does not retain raw CLI transcripts, model ID or cache-token counts. Metrics copied from its results.json; outputs and complete input workspaces retained.

The harness's practice-oriented grades are unsuitable for prose; preserved in results.json and harness-benchmark.json but superseded here. Do not use --rescore without a prose-aware grader, as it will overwrite this semantic aggregate.
